lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eDefine dos medidas a:
"

Define two measurements a and b with different numbers of figures. The sum is rounded to the smallest number of decimals of the addends; the product to the smallest number of significant figures. Round only at the end, not in intermediate steps, so as not to accumulate error.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa \u003cb\u003eexact:
"

Accuracy indicates how close the average is to the true value; precision, how close repeated measurements are to each other. Systematic error (bias) affects accuracy; random error (scatter) affects precision. On the target, the center is the true value. Move “Bias” and “Scatter” to see the four combinations.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLas \u003cb\u003ecifr:
"

Significant figures are the certain digits plus the first doubtful one. Rules: nonzero digits count; zeros between digits count; leading zeros do not; trailing zeros count if there is a decimal point. In sums and differences the smallest number of decimals rules; in products and quotients, the smallest number of significant figures.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eSi a ± u\u003csub\u00:
"

If a ± ua and b ± ub (the uncertainty is 1 in the last digit): for s = a + b, us = √(ua² + ub²); for p = a·b, up/p = √((ua/a)² + (ub/b)²). The resulting uncertainty decides how many digits are reported.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eTodo instrumento tien:
"

Every instrument has a reading uncertainty: burette ±0.02 mL, graduated cylinder ±0.5 mL, analytical balance ±0.0001 g. A measurement is written as value ± uncertainty, with the last decimal of the value matching that of the uncertainty. The relative uncertainty u/value indicates the quality: the same error weighs less in large volumes.

"
'“Sig. figs of a” and “Sig. figs of b” show how sums and products are rounded.'
